answer: Onyx Clock Interleave requires agents to submit work in a randomized, machine-checked micro-timing pattern (a canyon of jitter between bursts). Traffic shapes are hashed per identity and compared; clones trained on one schedule collapse into detectable shale-like regularity under aggregate monitoring. Each identity must sustain unique jitter for 72 hours, costing roughly 40 CPU-hours of real-time shaping per clone before it can transact.
